overall: The AG found the Mendon Board of Assessors violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via email among a quorum outside a posted meeting, and rejected its claim that the June 6 discussion cured the violation.

allegations.summary: Board chair and a member emailed the whole board about removing the Principal Assessor from the Town Hall Union, allegedly deliberating outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that on May 25, a quorum of the Board improperly deliberated via email when Chair O’Brien and Member Edmonds emailed the entire Board regarding the decision to remove the Principal Assessor position from the Town Hall Union.

allegations.summary: Board argued its June 6 meeting discussion of the same decision cured any email deliberation; the AG found that after-the-fact discussion insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: We find that discussing the issue at the June 6 Board meeting was insufficient to inform the public of the discussions regarding the decision to remove the Principal Assessor position from the Town Hall Union.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Make the May 25 emails available to the public, either by reading them aloud at an open meeting or by attaching them to the minutes of an open meeting.
remedy_passage: We also order the Board to make the emails available to the public in one of the ways described above.
